items.followUp: What information should you identify when analysing a problem?

rubric.why: Identifying the problem’s purpose or requirement is the first step in understanding it.
rubric.description: State that the problem should be analysed to determine what it requires.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the problem’s purpose, requirement, or what it asks.

rubric.why: Identifying the input and expected output clarifies what information the problem needs and produces.
rubric.description: Identify the input data and expected output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the input and output should be identified.

modelAnswer: Read and analyse the problem statement to understand what it requires.
Identify the input data and the expected output.

items.followUp: Write two advantages of using a flowchart.

rubric.why: Drawing a flowchart can take considerable time.
rubric.description: State that flowcharts take time to prepare.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the time required to draw a flowchart as a disadvantage.

rubric.why: Modifying a flowchart can be difficult, particularly when it is large or complex.
rubric.description: State that flowcharts are difficult to modify.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a flowchart is difficult to modify or change.

modelAnswer: They can be difficult to modify, especially when they are large or complex.

items.followUp: What happens to the contents of volatile memory when the power is switched off?

rubric.description: Identify volatile memory as temporary memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing volatile memory as temporary memory.

rubric.why: Volatile memory needs power to retain its contents.
rubric.description: State that its contents are lost when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that data or contents are lost when power is removed.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory is temporary memory that requires a continuous power supply.
Its contents are lost when the power is switched off.
